objections.claim: D-019 through D-023 are independently complete and independently revertible even though their operative text inherits the shared rationale/recording rule outside every entry, and D-020/D-022 additionally inherit D-019's three operative clauses.
objections.evidence: The shared rationale and shared recording rule are explicitly 'not itself a decision,' so neither has a C-D0xx commit, overturn rule, or specified durable placement in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. Every Route B entry depends on at least the shared recording rule; D-019 through D-022 also depend on the shared rationale. D-020 and D-022 do not state their operative clauses at all: they say 'Same three operative clauses as D-019.' Under D-000's commit-per-decision rule, committing the shared text with any one selector makes later selectors depend on that selector's revert unit; reverting it strands the remaining entries. Omitting the shared text leaves 'above' unresolved after an entry is copied into the coordinator register. Committing it separately contradicts the claim that it is not an entry/decision unless an exact non-decision carrier and persistence rule is recorded. Most directly, reverting C-D019 removes the live text D-020 and D-022 use to define their own decisions, so their promises that C-D020/C-D022 stand alone are false. A shared rationale may be non-decisional semantically; its bytes are still load-bearing operationally.
objections.proposedFix: Make each adopted entry self-contained: inline the recording rule and the relevant shared rationale, and write D-020/D-022's three clauses in full. Alternatively pin every inheritance to an immutable retained artifact path plus digest and state that the artifact survives every selector overturn; do not refer to a live sibling entry. Then define each C-D0xx commit so reverting any one leaves all other entries' complete operative bytes present and unambiguous.

objections.claim: The shared rationale accurately says the applied DR-002 through DR-008 successors are the rows D-019 through D-022 select.
objections.evidence: Applied DR-002..008 successors quantify over seven rows. D-019 through D-022 select four: DR-002, DR-004, DR-005, and DR-008's integration half. DR-003 is selected separately by D-023, while DR-006 and DR-007 remain preview rides and Route A work. The next sentence narrows none of this. The statement 'Those successors are the rows D-019..D-022 select' is therefore false as written and can be read as silently disposing DR-003/006/007 despite the row-specific entries saying otherwise.
objections.proposedFix: Say that D-019 through D-022 select the four authoritative evidence/custody rows within the seven-row DR-002..008 prerequisite set, then name DR-003's separate D-023 treatment and DR-006/DR-007's retained rides. Do not equate the four-row subset with the full successor range.

objections.claim: The amended Route C disjunction restates every lawful recording form: either the product authority records in the product-disposition packet, or the coordinator decides on the user's behalf under D-000 and records a D-000 entry.
objections.evidence: D-000's coordinator-register status vocabulary expressly defines ADOPTED as 'consensus reached or user-made,' and D-000 itself is an ADOPTED decision made directly by the user in conversation and recorded by the coordinator. A direct user-made product decision recorded in the coordinator register is neither branch of D-017's disjunction: it need not be a product-packet amendment, and the coordinator did not decide it on the user's behalf. The attempted repair therefore still narrows Route C while D-017 remains classified RULE-GOVERNED.
objections.proposedFix: Add the direct-user case: a product-authority packet/amendment, a decision made directly by the user and recorded in the coordinator register, or a coordinator decision made on the user's behalf under D-000. Preserve the distinction between recording a user decision and making one for the user.
